title: Qt: Have all DisplayFilterEdits have bookmarks
description:
Always add the bookmark button to a DisplayFilterEdit, such as
in the I/O Graphs dialog, the Coloring Rules dialog, etc.

Add a method to enable and disabled displaying bookmarks for,
e.g., the search frame which switches its line edit between
searching for display filters and other options (hex, string).

Make sure to update the filters if the app has been initialized
(we can't do this before it's been initialized, but DFEs from
other dialogs are created after initialization.)

Change the bookmark button placement from in the margin to the padding
of the box model, so that it works properly when contained in just
a DisplayFilterEdit and not a DisplayFilterCombo.

Only add the context menu item about the filter button preferences for
the main window display filter combobox to apply.

Fix #12028

notes.body:
added 7 commits
  • 59f0b0c7...dd316b00 - 6 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • dd893873 - Qt: Have all DisplayFilterEdits have bookmarks
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/16002/diffs?diff_id=1038283980&start_sha=59f0b0c705cb6579787373ca6579a5d783bd5ad3)

Need to fix some issues:
* The background of the bookmark button changes according to the filter, this should be unchanged
* The line separating the bookmark button is too long (a few pixels)
* The right line should not be there, or a clear button should be added 
* Should we also have the drop-down menu with history?
* In "Display Filter Expression" the bookmark button doesn't make sense because it's read-only
* "Remove this filter" does not work from all dialogs
* The bookmarked filters is not synchronised between all dialogs

![Screenshot_2024-07-06_at_14.26.24](/uploads/f90fbcad0693c06e374006409b064d11/Screenshot_2024-07-06_at_14.26.24.png)

> The background of the bookmark button changes according to the filter, this should be unchanged



> The line separating the bookmark button is too long (a few pixels)

This is because the `DisplayFilterEdit` doesn't have a border, the `DisplayFilterCombo` does, but the DFE is the one that draws the lines.

> The right line should not be there, or a clear button should be added

That one should be simple, don't draw the right line unless the clear button exists.

> Should we also have the drop-down menu with history?

Maybe, but the problem is that there's one big global list of filters. Using the combobox everywhere instead would be another way to address the border / line being too long, probably the background as well.

> "Remove this filter" does not work from all dialogs
> The bookmarked filters is not synchronised between all dialogs

This is related to a problem we have in a number of places - independent models onto the same file object. What we really in most cases should have is a single model that uses the file, and multiple views onto it. Then we wouldn't need to mess around with dialogs synchronizing manually.

> In "Display Filter Expression" the bookmark button doesn't make sense because it's read-only

Right. It would be kind of interesting if the bookmark could be used as a starting point, but it doesn't work because it's read-only.

> The background of the bookmark button changes according to the filter, this should be unchanged

Unfortunately, it seems like while `QComboBox` supports the `background-clip` [stylesheet property](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/stylesheet-reference.html#background-clip-prop), `QLineEdit` does not. So several of the problems would go away if we used the `DisplayComboBox` there.

> The line separating the bookmark button is too long (a few pixels)

An annoying issue is that there's no especially easy way to determine whether the `DisplayFilterEdit` is inside a `DisplayFilterCombo`, and no particular way that I can see to get "whatever the current border color is." We can set the border color in the `DisplayFilterEdit` to the same values used in `DisplayFilterCombo` and used for drawing that line, and then I think it looks better, at least consistent.

You do lose the standard effect of the border changing when a line edit is selected, e.g. being gray and then changing to blue, but that's hard to

!16312 should fix the third, fifth, sixth, and seventh issue mentioned there. To fix the background issue, we might have to do more overriding of the paintEvent, or else see if we can switch in general to using the ComboBox (which would also address the fourth issue.)
